results.title: Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
results.content: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

results.title: What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
results.content: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

results.title: Hungary eases abortion rules
results.content: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

results.title: Sri Lanka: Rights groups sound alarm over proposed anti-terror law
results.content: The Sri Lankan government is looking to replace a controversial anti-terror law but critics say the new one is just as bad.

results.title: UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
results.content: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

results.title: Jensen Huang: Spy row, second affair leaves Nvidia without its rockstar CEO
results.content: Jensen Huang, who built Nvidia into the world’s dominant AI chipmaker, is stepping down as CEO after a second affair came to light. DW examines how losing its figurehead will affect the firm and the US-China AI race.

results.title: Iran: Exiled journalists still repressed by regime
results.content: For many independent reporters, leaving Iran does not mean fully escaping the grasp of the Iranian state. The regime uses family members, bank accounts and the property they left behind to apply pressure across borders.

results.title: China's Xi Jinping renews calls for 'reunification' with Taiwan
results.content: Xi Jinping said that reunification was inevitable, but stopped short of mentioning military force. Taiwan though swiftly rejected Beijing's demands as tensions continue over the island's future.

results.title: Israel strikes Gaza hospital, says Hamas senior figure inside
results.content: Israel says Hamas was using the hospital as a military command center, while Palestinian officials report at least six people killed, including a surgeon. The strike comes amid an increasingly fragile ceasefire.

results.title: Brazil electoral court fines Meta, sees no deliberate election bias
results.content: The fine came after President Lula's coalition filed a complaint. The court said there was no evidence of intent to influence the election. Meta said it will defend itself against "false allegations."

results.title: Is AIIB's complaint mechanism failing affected communities?
results.content: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has a grievance redress mechanism for people affected by projects it finances. But those seeking to file a complaint face significant hurdles. Critics say reforms are needed.

results.title: Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
results.content: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.
